events.title: The Day the Music Died
events.description: A small plane crashed near Clear Lake, Iowa, killing rock and roll musicians Buddy Holly, Ritchie Valens, and J.P. 'The Big Bopper' Richardson, along with pilot Roger Peterson.
events.significance: The crash was a defining tragedy in early rock and roll history, cutting short the careers of three influential artists and later immortalized in Don McLean's song 'American Pie' (1971).

events.title: Ratification of the 16th Amendment
events.description: Delaware, Wyoming, and New Mexico's ratification brought the Sixteenth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution to the required number of states, authorizing Congress to levy a federal income tax without apportioning it among the states.
events.significance: The amendment fundamentally reshaped U.S. federal finance, enabling the modern income tax system that funds the federal government.

events.title: Ratification of the 15th Amendment
events.description: The Fifteenth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution was ratified, prohibiting the denial of voting rights based on race, color, or previous condition of servitude.
events.significance: It was a landmark Reconstruction-era achievement extending suffrage to Black men, though its promise was undermined for decades by discriminatory state practices until the Voting Rights Act of 1965.

events.title: Luna 9 Soft Lands on the Moon
events.description: The Soviet spacecraft Luna 9 became the first probe to achieve a controlled soft landing on the Moon and transmitted panoramic photographs from the lunar surface.
events.significance: The success proved the lunar surface could support a lander, providing crucial information for later crewed missions including Apollo.

events.title: Birth of Felix Mendelssohn
events.description: German composer, pianist, and conductor Felix Mendelssohn was born in Hamburg. He became a leading figure of the Romantic era, composing works such as A Midsummer Night's Dream overture and the Violin Concerto in E minor.
events.significance: Mendelssohn revived interest in the music of J.S. Bach and helped shape 19th-century concert life, including founding the Leipzig Conservatory.
